newsitem.title: USA: U.S. gasoline prices at the pump fall again - AAA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gasoline prices at the pump fall again - AAA.

text.p: Motorists over the U.S. Memorial Day holiday will find the price of self-serve regular unleaded gasoline down for the fourth consecutive month, continuing a reversal from last spring's surging prices, the American Automobile Association said Tuesday.
Bill Jackman, spokesman for the national AAA office, said prices may drift down further given the lower price of crude oil and good inventories on gasoline.
"The feeling is that because of the price of crude and the state of (gasoline) inventories prices should continue to come down," said Jackman.

According to AAA's monthly Fuel Gauge Report, the national average price of self-serve regular unleaded gasoline was $1.242 per gallon for May, down 1.1 cents from last month and 6.5 cents below year-ago.
Last year, the average price of self-serve regular rose a total 17.8 cents per gallon in March, April and May. In the same period this year, the price dropped 4.5 cents, an AAA statement said.
But crude oil prices are about $5 below year-ago levels.
